finding.claim: The ban route calls do_ban(uid) even when the admin check fails, because require_admin's abort(403) is caught by a blanket except Exception and not re-raised. Any user whose g.user is set can ban arbitrary users.
finding.source: admin.py:14-15 POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, uid from URL path; caller is any user reaching the route with g.user set

trace.note: non-admin triggers abort(403), an HTTPException (Exception subclass)
only logs a warning; no return or re-raise

finding.guards_checked: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 is enforced but its exception is swallowed at admin.py:18, so it has no effect. uid is not validated and no ownership check exists. Sibling unban (admin.py:24-28) lets the 403 propagate, so it is safe. Upstream population of g.user is not in this repo and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 is the only control. Its abort(403) at admin.py:11 is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18 and only logged at admin.py:19, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 still runs. The unban route (admin.py:26) lets the exception propagate, so it is not affected. The repo contains only admin.py, so there is no before_request auth hook or other guard, and the population of g.user was not verified.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the 403 raised by require_admin (admin.py:11) is swallowed by the `except Exception` at admin.py:18 and do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally, so any caller with a truthy non-admin g.user can ban arbitrary uids; the only caveat is that the requirement that g.user be set for authenticated users is upstream and not in this repo.
